name: Snake River — Jackson Lake Dam to Wilson (Grand Teton NP)
blurb: Snake River below Jackson Lake Dam through Grand Teton National Park to the Wilson bridge; braided channels and logjams on the lower stretches (NPS).

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.notes: Scenic, calmer water and few obstructions. Water is swift at Pacific Creek landing; scout the landing before launching (NPS). Put-in Dam (Snake): exact agency facility pin. Take-out Pacific Creek (Snake): exact agency facility pin. Grand Teton boat permit: "All watercraft —motorized and non-motorized, including SUPs and windsurfing boards— must have a valid Grand Teton Boat Permit." Privately owned vessels must register each year (Recreation.gov or park visitor centres), and a Wyoming Aquatic Invasive Species decal is required unless the craft is exempt. Non-motorized inflatables 10 feet or shorter, paddleboards and water-sport toys are exempt from the state decal, but inspection requirements still apply. Wyoming: next to private land the streambed is private — no anchoring, wading or getting out without landowner permission; floating through is legal. Watercraft entering Wyoming Mar 1–Nov 30 need an AIS inspection. Mileage: NPS Grand Teton float page.

notices.title: Grand Teton boating rules
notices.text: A park boat permit is required. Inner tubes, air mattresses and float tubes are prohibited on the Snake River in the park and parkway. Scout landings, check current river conditions and stop at open AIS inspection stations. Use the designated boat launch below Jackson Lake Dam; floating within 1,000 feet of the dam is prohibited.

sections.notes: The most challenging stretch in the park; many accidents occur here. Steeper drop, faster current, complex braiding and side channels blocked by logjams (NPS). Put-in Deadman's (Snake): exact agency facility pin. Take-out Moose (Snake): exact agency facility pin. Grand Teton boat permit: "All watercraft —motorized and non-motorized, including SUPs and windsurfing boards— must have a valid Grand Teton Boat Permit." Privately owned vessels must register each year (Recreation.gov or park visitor centres), and a Wyoming Aquatic Invasive Species decal is required unless the craft is exempt. Non-motorized inflatables 10 feet or shorter, paddleboards and water-sport toys are exempt from the state decal, but inspection requirements still apply. NPS: Deadmans Bar to Moose and Moose to Wilson are advanced water with braided channels and logjams; there is no take-out at the park boundary below Moose — the next take-out is the Wilson bridge, 14 miles below Moose. Wyoming: next to private land the streambed is private — no anchoring, wading or getting out without landowner permission; floating through is legal. Watercraft entering Wyoming Mar 1–Nov 30 need an AIS inspection. Mileage: NPS Grand Teton float page.
